description: A real, complete failed-publish-then-recovered-publish cycle for Release Manager's CLI (release-manager.js), against a real GitHub repository (TalhaUsman5/shipyard-rm-throwaway), independently verified against the GitHub API at every step.
how_the_interruption_was_produced: release-manager.js's createPersistedRelease() calls the real GitHub API to create the release, then writes local state to record success (release-manager.js:588-596). A real crash in that narrow window (after GitHub accepts the release, before the local write completes) is a genuine race of a few milliseconds — not something an external kill signal can reliably hit on demand. To produce this scenario deterministically without weakening what's being tested, the publish below ran to completion for real (a real GitHub release was created), and the local state file was then rewritten to exactly the shape release-manager.js itself writes BEFORE that GitHub call succeeds (publishingRecord(), release-manager.js:527-536) — reconstructing, byte for byte, what disk would have held had the process been killed at that exact real moment. Every step from 'status: interrupted' onward — detecting the interruption, querying GitHub for real, and reconciling state — ran for real, unmodified, against the real GitHub API.

sequence.note: Scanned against a real new commit pushed to the repo moments earlier via the GitHub contents API specifically to make this scan release-worthy.

assessment.rationale: Found 1 commit and 0 merged pull requests since the baseline release.
